title: PostgreSQL internals, Part 3: VACUUM and bloat
tldr: How PostgreSQL cleans up the row versions MVCC leaves behind: VACUUM's three phases, dead line pointers, the free space and visibility maps, HOT updates and on-access pruning, measuring the HOT ratio and choosing fillfactor, autovacuum's trigger formula and cost-based throttling, measuring table and index bloat with pgstattuple, VACUUM FULL against pg_repack and REINDEX CONCURRENTLY, freezing and transaction ID wraparound, two real wraparound outages, and a decision table plus interview drill.
